title: Implement Configurable Default Log Level
description: ChronoFlow Nexus is a high-performance C++ microservice. Currently, its logging level is hardcoded, making it difficult to adjust verbosity in different environments (e.g., verbose DEBUG logs in development vs. concise ERROR logs in production) without recompiling. This multi-session task involves introducing a new configuration option to control the application's default log level.

project_spec.name: ChronoFlow Nexus
project_spec.description:
ChronoFlow Nexus is a high-performance C++ microservice dedicated to boosting enterprise productivity by orchestrating time-tracking, task analytics, and team workload insights through a single, versioned API layer. The service exposes both REST endpoints and a GraphQL schema so client applications—ranging from calendar widgets to Kanban dashboards—can query exactly the data they need, eliminate over-fetching, and remain extremely responsive on any device. ChronoFlow Nexus embodies a finely grained layered architecture: transport, interface, application, domain, and infrastructure layers keep responsibilities isolated, enabling rapid feature evolution without jeopardizing system stability. 

Designed for hard-scale environments, the project integrates response caching, adaptive rate limiting, and request validation to guarantee consistent latency even under unpredictable traffic bursts. Built-in observability (metrics, structured logging, tracing) and an API gateway façade ensure that operations teams can deploy, monitor, and roll out new versions independently, while developers iterate on productivity-centric features—like real-time focus analytics—behind a robust Command–Query Separation boundary.

With 67 thoughtfully organized source files and roughly 370 k tokens of code, ChronoFlow Nexus stands apart from typical microservice examples by focusing obsessively on the productivity domain: every endpoint (REST and GraphQL) surfaces KPIs such as time-on-task, context-switch frequency, and flow-state interruptions, empowering organizations to remove friction and maximize deep-work hours.
dependencies: graphqlcpp (or diy GraphQL parser) – GraphQL Schema execution
cpp_redis + Redis – response caching and rate-limiter buckets
libpqxx – PostgreSQL access via Repository pattern
C++17 STL & filesystem – core language/library features
